children: By Staff Writer

Economic experts have said that reforms introduced by the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Mr Olayemi Cardoso, have pulled the nation’s economy back from severe structural instability and repositioned it on the path of sustainable growth.

The experts, who spoke in separate interviews with the Nigerian Tribune in Abuja, said Cardoso’s focus on orthodox monetary policy has restored credibility to the apex bank, reversed macro-economic instability and built robust external buffers.

An economic expert and financial services consultant, Mr Eric Igulla, noted that the CBN governor successfully unified the country’s chaotic multiple exchange rate windows, cleared the crippling $7 billion inherited foreign exchange backlog and established an open, electronic market-driven matching framework.
Igulla commended the Cardoso administration for the ongoing banking sector recapitalisation exercise, which he described as a massive overhaul.

According to him, “A massive overhaul forced commercial banks to shore up capital bases, up to N500 billion for international licences, raising over N4.65 trillion in fresh capital to insulate the financial system from structural shocks.

“Through decisive monetary tightening, including an 850 basis point interest rate hike over a nine-month period, the CBN curbed soaring numbers, bringing headline inflation down significantly to its lowest levels in three years,” Igulla stated.
The apex bank also disclosed that under Cardoso, far-reaching foreign exchange market reforms have been implemented to enhance transparency and stability.

Under the 2026 Bureau De Change (BDC) market reforms, licensed BDCs gained structured access to foreign exchange through authorised dealer banks, supported by the FX BDC Purchase Tracker for enhanced transparency, compliance and real-time oversight.

Similarly, under the International Oil Companies (IOCs) export-proceeds reform, IOCs are now permitted to repatriate 100 per cent of export proceeds through authorised dealer banks, further liberalising the FX market, while the diaspora remittance reform introduced new naira-settlement requirements for International Money Transfer Operators to improve transparency and traceability of remittance flows.

Another expert, Mr Moses Epelle of Suraj Enterprises, said the recognition of the CBN as Central Bank of the Year by the Central Banking International publication and the Distinguished Organisation Award by the Nigerian Economic Society (NES) are indications that the governor is on the right track.

Epelle applauded the CBN for the definitive cessation of the controversial Ways and Means financing, a practice he said had previously flooded the economy with trillions in unauthorised currency and stoked inflation.

He said: “Driven by a transparent framework and a spike in diaspora remittances, nearing $1 billion monthly by mid-2026, Nigeria’s external reserves comfortably crossed the $50 billion threshold, offering immense import cover.

“The structural overhaul has re-anchored global trust, as reflected in notable global recognitions. Global rating bodies like Fitch, Moody’s and S&P upgraded Nigeria’s credit ratings and economic outlooks due to macroeconomic resilience.”

Analysts also cited the Payments System Vision 2028 as a strategic roadmap anchored on Interoperability, Security, Inclusion, Innovation, Trust and Collaboration, positioning Nigeria’s payments system for a more secure, inclusive and globally integrated digital economy.

They noted that reforms such as the Revised Agent Banking Guidelines have resulted in stronger consumer protection, agent oversight, transaction controls, geo-location requirements and sanctions, while initiatives like the Point-of-Sale (PoS), Geo-Fencing and Dual Connectivity measures have improved traceability, resilience and reliability of PoS transactions.

According to the CBN, the new cash-withdrawal thresholds introduced, alongside the removal of restrictions and charges on cash deposits, have supported more efficient cash management and digital payment adoption in the country.

The apex bank also, in 2026, launched a Faster Anti-Fraud Response, directing banks to strengthen rapid-response mechanisms for electronic fraud, with emphasis on significantly reducing intervention time, while in March 2026, it introduced the Bank Verification Number (BVN) and Watchlist Framework for identity verification, with watchlist controls enhanced to combat fraud and strengthen the integrity of the banking system.
Analysts believe that, taken together, the reforms have put the Nigerian economy firmly on the path of growth in the coming months.

title: ZAWYA: From $7bln FX backlog to $50bln reserves: Experts credit Cardoso’s Central Bank of Nigeria reforms for economic turnaround
